messages.content: I'm planning a camping trip and I need to know the weather forecast. Can you fetch me the weather data for the campsite located at latitude 35.68 and longitude -121.34 for the next 10 days including daily temperature and precipitation forecasts? Also, I prefer the temperature 2 minute max in Fahrenheit and sum of precipitation in inches.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

We have to use the tool `requests_get` from the defined namespace. We want to get weather forecast for coordinates 35.68,-121.34 for next 10 days. Need daily temp and precip. Temperature 2 min max in Fahrenheit; sum of precipitation in inches.

Which API can provide this? Possibly open-meteo.com provides free endpoints. But we don't see instructions about using external APIs. However we might call some generic endpoint like "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". Let's check typical usage:

GET /v1/forecast?latitude=...&longitude=...&daily=temperature_2m_max,precipitation_sum&timezone=auto&start_date=YYYY-MM-DD&end_date=YYYY-MM-DD

But we also need units: For temperature in Fahrenheit, maybe set parameter &units=imperial? Actually open-meteo uses metric by default; there may be param "temperature_unit=fahrenheit"? Wait open-meteo has "temperature_units": "fahrenheit", "metric" etc. Let’s search memory: open-meteo supports "temperature_unit=fahrenheit" or "temperature_unit=celsius".

Also precipitation unit: "precipitation_unit=inches" ?

Let's recall: In open-meteo docs, they support "temperature_unit=fahrenheit" and "windspeed_unit=mph" etc. Precipitation unit likely "precipitation_unit=inch" or "inches". Not sure exactly. Might just return mm by default; we could convert ourselves. But requirement says sum of precipitation in inches. So either specify unit or compute conversion after retrieving mm.

Better to ask them to retrieve precipitation in inches via param "precipitation_unit=inch" or "precipitation_unit=mm"? We'll guess "precipitation_unit=inch".

Ok.

Now we need start_date today. Use today's date. Today is unknown; let's assume current date is 2026-05-16. Next 10 days includes 2026-05-17 through 2026-05-26 inclusive. Provide end_date accordingly.

Thus build url: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=35.68&longitude=-121.34&daily=temperature_2m_max,precipitation_sum&start_date=2026-05-17&end_date=2026-05-26&timezone=America/Los_Angeles&temperature_unit=fahrenheit&precipitation_unit=inch

Add timezone param to ensure local times.

We'll produce JSON output.

So call the tool with params dict containing all those fields. Since our custom function expects separate keys for each param group: e.g., "lat","lon","format"... but we can't pass arbitrary query strings beyond those recognized. Our function signature only allows certain known query parameters: lat, lon, format. That means we cannot directly supply other query parameters such as daily, start_date, etc. Because the function definition restricts allowed query parameters to {lat?, lon?, format?}. That's limiting. Maybe we can circumvent by passing raw URL with full query string appended manually. The function accepts "url:" field where we can include entire query string. Then "params?" optional additional ones. But we can embed everything into url itself. Yes.

Therefore we'll construct full URL with query string embedded.

Hence call:

function calls: 
{
"url":"https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=35.68&longitude=-121.34&daily=temperature_2m_max%2Cprecipitation_sum&start_date=2026-05-17&end_date=2026-05-26&timezone=America%2FLos_Angeles&temperature_unit=fahrenheit&precipitation_unit=inch",
"headers":{"Accept":"application/json"},
"timeout":5.0,
"allow_redirects":true
}

No need for auth/cert/proxy.

Return result.

Will do so.
